mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds rate above 2% for two consecutive months reduces the discount rate applied to future equity cash flows, lowering the present value of expected dividends and earnings, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 2% and remains above for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive or flat when the trigger is active, or the discount rate sensitivity to FEDFUNDS is estimated below 0.5% per percentage point increase.

mechanism_narrative: Rising monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which increases consumer confidence and corporate earnings expectations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while UNRATE decreases over the same month
failure_condition: The interaction term between PAYEMS growth and UNRATE is statistically insignificant (p > 0.05) or 60-day forward returns are not meaningfully higher than during a non-strengthening labor period.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in personal consumption expenditures (CPIAUCSL) relative to GDP (GDPC1) indicates excess demand in the economy, prompting firms to raise prices and expand output, which is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL growth rate exceeds 2% while GDPC1 growth rate is below 1% in the same month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative despite the signal, or the CPI/GDP ratio momentum is not statistically significant (Rank IC > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) accompanied by a decline in consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL) suggests supply-side constraints, reducing near-term earnings expectations and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by more than 3% while CPIAUCSL declines by at least 0.5% in the same month
regime_hint: supply shock or weakening production capacity
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when the signal is present, or the interaction is not robust across multiple rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the 2-year Treasury yield (implied by FEDFUNDS dynamics) over three consecutive months lowers the real discount rate, increasing the present value of future equities and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are flat or negative despite the sustained yield decline, or the discount rate sensitivity exceeds 1% per percentage point decline in yield.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in job openings (HOUST) without a corresponding rise in job vacancies (PAYEMS) indicates a labor market imbalance favoring supply, which can trigger a risk-off reaction and produce negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by >10% in a single month while PAYEMS increases by <2% in the same month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when the signal occurs, or the HOUST/PAYEMS ratio momentum is not statistically significant.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 4% for the first time in three months while the Federal Funds rate remains unchanged, it signals a shift to a more expansionary policy regime, which is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses below 4% and remains below for at least three months while FEDFUNDS is steady
regime_hint: near-labor-market-full employment combined with steady monetary policy
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not positive when the trigger is met, or the interaction is not significant in a two-tailed test (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in both industrial production (INDPRO) and consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL) suggests weakening demand-side pressures while supply remains constrained, lowering growth expectations and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not negative when both indicators show the described pattern, or the interaction term is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
